## Super 66 (Tatts Rules Schedule B)

- fixed divisions return $0.4764 per $1 game (Div 2-5 fixed at $6,666/$666/$66/$6.60 with odds 1 in 55,556/5,556/556/56)
- games per draw (bloc, Div-5 winners x 56): ~369,286; observed Division 1 accrual $48,407/draw (draw 4715 paid $193,627 after 4 accruing draws), i.e. ~$0.131/game -> implied prize fund ~61% of the $1 retail price
- P(no Div-1 winner in a draw) = 0.691; mean cycle 3.2 draws; break-even jackpot (retail $1.00, with sharing at current sales) = $626,193 -> needs ~13 accruing draws; P(cycle gets there) = 0.96% (~0.15 times per year at current sales)
- largest jackpot found: $380,724 (22 Jul 2017, lotteryguru); recent wins $193,627 and $123,418 (API). Falling sales lengthen cycles and make break-even MORE likely over time.
- roll-down clause: Schedule B r.4.4-4.6 after 26 consecutive carry-overs; P(26 straight no-win draws) = 6.76e-05. Cover-all of 1,000,000 combos costs $1,000,000 and returns $476,420 fixed + jackpot x 0.84 (sharing).

## Effect of choosing unpopular combinations (pari-mutuel Division 1)

Expected share of a Division 1 pool = (1-exp(-lam))/lam where lam = expected number of OTHER winning games holding your combination. If your combination is chosen r times as often as average, lam = r x (games sold / N).
Because ~70% of entries are terminal-generated quick picks (uniform), r cannot realistically go below ~0.75 (0.70 + 0.30 x a very unpopular self-pick); r=0.5 is an optimistic bound.

Powerball break-even requires J x share_factor >= (retail - lower) x N = $145M of *effective* (post-sharing) jackpot; observed sales make share_factor ~0.4-0.6 above $100M, so the effective jackpot tops out near $75-80M.
Oz Lotto break-even: J x share_factor >= $64M effective; the $100M draw of 4 Feb 2025 reached ~$51M effective (closest any Australian jackpot game has come).
Roll-down after 25 consecutive jackpots (Tatts Schedules C/E, SA Powerball Rules, NSW rules): the $200M Powerball run was ~7 draws; the record Oz Lotto run found was 9 weeks. P(25 straight no-win draws | lambda>=0.25 each) <= 1.9e-03; with sales growth it is far smaller.

## Fixed-prize games

- Set for Life: prize fund capped at 40% of subscriptions (Schedule H 1.2(b)); Div 1 = $200k + $20k/month x 240 (PV at 4.9% p.a. ~ $3.28M) at 1 in 38,320,568 = $0.086 per $0.80 game; shared only above 4 winners. RTP ~40%: worst value, no lever.
- Weekday Windfall: Div 1 fixed $1,000,000 per winner up to 6 winners ($6M shared beyond), from reserve, not pari-mutuel (Schedule D 4.3(a)); prize fund for Div 2-6 only 33%. Div 1 EV = $1M/8,145,060 = $0.123 per ~$0.67 game (18%) + ~33% x subscription -> RTP ~ 48%; 'Double Win Day' doubles Div 2-6 pools -> ~77%.
